key_insight: High-dimensional function approximation admits a lattice-ball regime with expense scaling as d^(R²)/(R²!), polynomial in dimension d for fixed R, when R² ≪ d.
engineering_relevance: In this regime, spectral approximations can require substantially fewer terms than hypercube scaling R^d suggests, potentially reducing high-dimensional modeling costs.
method: Approximate analytic or m-times continuously differentiable functions using orthogonal series.
Use Fourier, Chebyshev, or Legendre expansions.
Analyze expense by counting lattice points inside a hypersphere.
evidence_signal: Numerical illustrations cover MNIST digit classification and learning solution operators for Burgers’ and radiative transfer equations; the abstract reports no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: The favorable scaling requires R² ≪ d and does not imply dimension-independent cost or removal of the curse in every approximation regime.
paper_title: Second scaling regime in high-dimensional function approximation and curse of dimensionality
